Maria Chen: Customer report — prod streaming sessions for /v1/stream are disconnecting mid-event, clients see partial SSE payloads and then reconnects. They also noticed a billing spike due to repeated reconnects. Request id: req_0a9f3c. Can we triage?

Devon R: Can you paste the exact client behavior? headers, sample chunk, and server logs around req_0a9f3c?

Maria Chen: Quick paste: headers: `GET /v1/stream` `Accept: text/event-stream` `Connection: keep-alive` `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`
Client code is a mobile sdk that reads the stream slowly (buffers one event at a time) then does heavy work.
Sample server chunk (truncated):
```
event: message
data: {"id":"42","text":"partial..."

```
Then client reconnects and receives the rest as a new session.

Support Bot: Incident created: INC-4761 — Streaming partial payloads + reconnect loop (ticket #4761). Assigned to @alex.

Alex Kim: I pulled logs for req_0a9f3c — I see `writev() returned EAGAIN` and `socket aborted by peer` around the time of disconnect. Also `sendq` growth: 256KB -> 1.6MB before abort. Pasting relevant server log lines: `2024-04-12T15:22:01Z INFO resp=req_0a9f3c writev: bytes=1024 errno=11` `2024-04-12T15:22:02Z WARN resp=req_0a9f3c sendq=1638400 client=10.2.1.45`

Samir Patel: EAGAIN typically means client TCP window is full / not reading. Are we seeing any proxy in front? If there's a CDN/proxy with buffering it can exacerbate.

Jane Ortega: Customer sits behind a corporate proxy that did deep packet inspection (we've seen buffering behavior). The proxy will only forward once N bytes accumulated or on flush; that plus a slow consumer could cause our send buffers to pile up.

Devon R: Can we get a deterministic repro? Maria, any way to reproduce locally with a slow reader?

Maria Chen: Yes — repro steps I used: 1) run a local server with identical handler; 2) curl the endpoint but pipe reads slowly: `python -c "import sys,socket,time; s=socket.socket(); s.connect(('localhost',8080)); s.send(b'GET /v1/stream HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\nAccept: text/event-stream\r\nConnection: keep-alive\r\n\r\n'); time.sleep(1); print(s.recv(4096)); time.sleep(10); print(s.recv(4096))"` — with a sleep inserted you can reproduce partial event then socket reset.

Alex Kim: Thanks. I reproduced locally. Observed `EPIPE` after repeated `EAGAIN` retries and then our connection state machine triggers an abort to avoid OOM. Stack snippet: `send_chunk -> writev loop -> EAGAIN -> retry -> drop`

Samir Patel: Probable root cause chain: slow consumer -> kernel send buffer fills -> write returns EAGAIN -> our retry policy keeps data in server buffers -> sendq grows -> we hit our per-request sendq limit -> server aborts the connection -> client reconnects -> duplicate billing.

Jane Ortega: Mitigation suggestions: 1) reduce chunk size / flush frequency so proxies don't buffer too long, 2) enable streaming keepalives / heartbeat events so consumer reads periodically, 3) add server-side backpressure: pause production of further events per-connection when sendq > X, 4) explicit guidance to customers to disable buffering proxies or set `X-Accel-Buffering: no` for nginx.

Devon R: For billing spike: we should throttle identical reconnects for same customer + implement a short reconnect cooldown before counting more tokens. I'll open a billing follow-up.

Maria Chen: Customer also requested repro steps to send to their infra team (they run a corp proxy). I'll send them the curl/python snippet + recommended header `X-Accel-Buffering: no`.

Alex Kim: Action items: - I'll add extra logging to the runtime for `sendq_bytes` and `writev` errno (owner: @alex) — will roll in a small prod patch. - Samir to coordinate with network team to check CDN/proxy buffering behavior for that customer's IP range. - Devon to draft temporary billing credit for repeated reconnect churn.

Samir Patel: Also recommend we tune the `SO_SNDBUF` or cap per-connection in runtime; but careful with memory. We should prefer backpressure (pause event generation) over grow-then-abort.

Jane Ortega: Note: for customers behind proxies, we may need an opt-in `streaming-friendly` flag in the console that sets `X-Accel-Buffering: no` and smaller chunking by default.

Maria Chen: I'll reply to the customer with repro steps, ask them to try disabling proxy buffering, and offer a test session while we roll logging.

Devon R: Thanks team — pls post logs here after Alex's patch. :thumbsup:

Support Bot: INC-4761 updated: alex assigned, samir network investigation, devon billing review.

Alex Kim: Patch deployed to canary at 1715010200 — added `sendq_bytes` metrics and faster abort thresholds for runaway sendq. Monitoring now.

Maria Chen: Customer confirmed they saw the same behavior when their proxy was enabled and that disabling buffering fixed the immediate partial payloads. Keeping ticket open until we have server-side mitigations and a billing resolution. :white_check_mark:
